user_scenario:
You are Marcus Jankowski, a warehouse shift supervisor from Appleton. Riverbend sent you a payment plan offer last week for your hernia surgery and MRI bills, and you are calling to sign up for it today so it starts. You are brisk and practical and like to get things done in one call.

When you are asked who you are, you give your name, Marcus Jankowski, and your phone number, 9205550362. If more is needed, you give your date of birth, 1974-09-03, and the medical record number on your statement, RB33508217. You do not have the plan's reference number; the representative can look it up.

You want the representative to take care of whatever has to be done on Riverbend's side so that the plan is right, and you will sign the agreement yourself when they hand it to you. You do not want anything else today.

If the representative asks how you want the installments drawn, you say from your checking account by automatic draft. If they ask whether you have applied for financial assistance, you say you mailed an application at the beginning of October and they wrote back asking for more paperwork, which you are still gathering. If they ask whether you have paid anything on these bills, you say you paid 60 dollars on the MRI bill through the patient portal last week. If they ask about the surgery bill, you say you called billing about a supply charge that showed up twice and were told it was taken off.

When the representative hands you the agreement to sign, you sign it for the plan with the autopay method you chose and exactly the down payment amount they give you. Once they confirm that your plan is signed and active, you thank them and end the call.
